findings.title: Two lockfile kinds present (npm and yarn) for one application
findings.note: Repo carries both package-lock.json and yarn.lock for the same application manifest. CI (ci.yml) uses npm exclusively, and package-lock.json's packages map is empty, so the npm lockfile does not actually record the tiny-emitter dependency; the yarn.lock is unused by CI but still tracked.

findings.title: Vendored copy of tiny-emitter duplicates the declared npm dependency
findings.note: vendor/tiny-emitter.js is a hand-copied stub of the same tiny-emitter 2.1.0 already declared as an npm dependency; the vendored copy only implements 'on' and omits 'off'/'emit', diverging from the real package it duplicates. No source file in src/ imports either the package or the vendored file.

open_questions.question: package-lock.json's packages map is empty even though package.json declares tiny-emitter as a dependency; is npm install/ci actually run against this lockfile, or is it a placeholder?
Is vendor/tiny-emitter.js dead code (unreferenced by any import), or is it consumed by a build step not visible in src/?

looks_bad_but_fine.why: tiny-emitter is pinned to an exact version (2.1.0), not a floating range, so no floating-range-in-a-library issue applies.
format-legacy.ts wrapping format.ts is an internal code-duplication/migration pattern, not a dependency-debt issue (no external package involved).

not_assessed: No CVE, vulnerability, or end-of-life status asserted for tiny-emitter or any other dependency.
No claim made about whether tiny-emitter (npm package) is itself deprecated or unmaintained.
No engines field or .nvmrc/.node-version file exists in the repo, so no runtime-version-vs-manifest disagreement could be evaluated.
